Theme

Latin word

habeō

habeō, habēre, habuī, habitum

verb, second conjugation, with prō and the ablative

consider, regard (someone or something as …); have (something) done, found out, settled (cognitum habeō); have; hold (a meeting); I have to, I must; I have (something) to say, I can say

In this lexicon

  • consider

    the recommended word · classical · Caes. BG 1.44: sēsē illum nōn prō amīcō, sed prō hoste habitūrum; Cic. Att. 13.1.2: istuc jam prō factō habeō; Traupman 296, 406

  • have

    also used · classical · Sall. Cat. 58.1: compertum ego habeō (Lewis & Short); Cic. Fam. 13.17.3: sī nōndum eum satis habēs cognitum (Lewis & Short); Traupman 326

  • have

    the recommended word · classical · Phaedr. 4.25.16–21: cum opus est, nīl habēs; Traupman 326

  • hold

    also used · classical · Traupman 328

  • must

    avoid · late Latin · Varr. RR 1.1.2: rogās, ut id mihi habeam cūrāre (Lewis & Short s.v. habeō); Lact. 4.12.15 (Lewis & Short)

  • say

    also used · classical · Cic. Att. 2.22.6: dē rē pūblicā nihil habeō ad tē scrībere (Lewis & Short s.v. habeō); Cic. Rosc. Am. 100: habeō etiam dīcere (Lewis & Short); Traupman 100: this I have to say, haec habeō dīcere; Traupman 326

  • persuāsum habeō: convince

    classical

  • mihi nōn bene habeō: feel

    modern

  • Mē male habeō.: I don’t feel well

    classical

  • Melius mē habeō.: I feel better

    classical

  • Mē bene habeō.: I’m fine

    classical

  • Grātiam habeō (maximam).: thank you

    classical
